newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle crew set for Thursday landing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle crew set for Thursday landing.

text.p: The astronauts aboard the U.S. space shuttle Columbia were making final preparations on Thursday for their return to earth after a successful 16-day science mission.
Columbia, the oldest shuttle in NASA's fleet, was to make a fiery hour-long descent through the atmosphere and touch down at Florida's Kennedy Space shortly after sunrise at 6:47 a.m. EDT (1047 GMT).
Columbia's clamlike cargo bay doors were swung shut for landing at about 3 a.m. EDT (0700 GMT) as the astronauts packed away the last of their gear.
Weather conditions looked favourable for the shuttle's homecoming, although there was a slight chance of patchy ground fog, NASA mission control commentator Kyle Herring said.
"At the present time, we do have a go forecast for this morning's landing," he said.
If necessary, the shuttle had a second landing opportunity one orbit of the earth later at 8:22 a.m. EDT (1222 GMT).
The shuttle's bus-sized space laboratory, which for the past 16 days was the venue for a $86 million research programme, was closed on Wednesday.
Columbia's seven astronauts completed work left unfinished in April, when the shuttle had to return to earth 12 days early because of a defective power generator.
It was the first time NASA had sent a shuttle and its crew back to space to complete a mission.
Since blasting off on July 1, Columbia's crew performed more than 30 experiments and ignited 206 controlled fires for combustion research, 42 more than originally planned.
